newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-WOODBRIDGE AND DRAPER PRODUCE AUSTRALIAN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-WOODBRIDGE AND DRAPER PRODUCE AUSTRALIAN FINAL.

text.p: Australian Todd Woodbridge, one half of the best doubles combination in the world, enhanced his singles reputation on Saturday by reaching the Australian Hardcourt final.
Compatriot Scott Draper guaranteed a home winner in the ATP event by winning his semifinal in stifling temperatures of 38 degress centigrade at Adelaide Oval.
Woodbridge, the fourth seed, fought back after losing a first set tie break to beat unseeded Swede Mikael Tillstrom 6-7 (6-8) 7-6 (7-3) 6-3.
Woodbridge, ranked 36 in the world and best known for his successful doubles partnership with fellow Australian Mark Woodforde, has said he will concentrate on improving his singles ranking in 1997.
Unseeded Draper was also taken to three sets before accounting for American qualifier Jeff Tarango 6-1 3-6 6-2.
It will be Woodbridge's eighth career singles final, while Draper has never before reached this stage of an ATP tournament.
The Australian recorded his only singles triumph in May 1995 when he won the Red Clay championships at Coral Springs in the United States.
